config.title: Flex order

intro.title: Flex order
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple navigation bar with three items and learn how to rearrange their visual order using CSS Flexbox. You will explore the `order` property, which allows you to control the sequence of flex items without changing the HTML structure. The main technologies involved are CSS Flexbox and the `order` property. This beginner-friendly lesson will help you understand how to visually reorder elements to improve layout design.
intro.usecase: The flex order property is essential for responsive layouts where content needs to rearrange based on screen size. In product dashboards, key metrics often move to the top on mobile while remaining in sidebars on desktop. E-commerce sites use it to prioritize product images over descriptions on smaller screens, and form builders reorder input fields for better mobile usability. Developers frequently apply flex order to create adaptive navigation menus, card layouts, and content panels that maintain logical flow across devices.

objectives: Apply the order property to flex items to rearrange their visual sequence
Configure multiple flex items with different order values to create custom layouts
Manipulate the default order of flex items to override the source order
Integrate the order property with other flexbox properties for responsive designs
Construct a flex container where items are visually reordered without changing HTML structure
Update the visual hierarchy of elements using positive, negative, and zero order values
Control the stacking of flex items when order values are equal

steps.title: Create a container with display: flex
steps.instruction: Create a CSS rule for a .container class that sets display to flex.
steps.hint: Start by writing .container { } and inside the curly braces, add display: flex;
steps.expectedOutcome: A .container class is created with display: flex, establishing a flex container.
successCriteria: The .container rule exists and contains display: flex;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've written .container { } with display: flex; inside.
steps.feedbackWrong: Create a CSS rule for .container that sets display to flex.

steps.title: Add flex items with basic styling
steps.instruction: Create CSS rules for three flex item classes: .item1, .item2, and .item3. Give each a width of 100px, height of 100px, a distinct background color, and a margin of 10px.
steps.hint: Define each class separately with the same width, height, and margin values, but use different background colors (like red, green, blue) to distinguish them.
steps.expectedOutcome: Three CSS class rules are created with consistent dimensions and spacing but different colors, ready to be applied to flex items.
successCriteria: CSS rules for .item1, .item2, and .item3 exist, each with width: 100px, height: 100px, a background-color, and margin: 10px.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that all three classes have width: 100px, height: 100px, a background-color, and margin: 10px.
steps.feedbackWrong: This step requires creating three CSS class rules (.item1, .item2, .item3) with the specified dimensions, colors, and margin.

steps.title: Set initial order values for flex items
steps.instruction: Add the CSS property order: 0 to all three item classes (.item1, .item2, .item3) to explicitly set their initial order values.
steps.hint: Add 'order: 0;' inside each of the three item class rules. This makes the default order explicit.
steps.expectedOutcome: All three flex items will have their order explicitly set to 0, establishing their default visual order.
successCriteria: The CSS rules for .item1, .item2, and .item3 each contain 'order: 0;'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added order: 0 to some items, but not all three. Make sure .item1, .item2, and .item3 each have this property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The order property isn't correctly added to all three items. Each item class needs 'order: 0;' inside its CSS rule.

steps.title: Change the order of the second item
steps.instruction: In the .item2 selector, set the order property to 1.
steps.hint: The order property accepts integer values. Setting it to 1 will visually move the second item to the end of the flex container.
steps.expectedOutcome: The second flex item will appear at the end of the container due to its higher order value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've set order: 1 specifically in the .item2 selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added the order property with a value of 1 to the correct selector (.item2).

steps.title: Change the order of the first item
steps.instruction: Change the order property for .item1 to 2 so it appears after .item2 in the flex container.
steps.hint: Look for the .item1 selector in your CSS and modify its order value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The first flex item (.item1) will visually appear after the second item (.item2) due to its higher order value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're modifying the .item1 selector specifically and setting order: 2.
steps.feedbackWrong: The order property for .item1 wasn't changed correctly. Check that you're using the right selector and value.

steps.title: Use negative order values
steps.instruction: Change the order value for .item3 to -1 to move it to the beginning of the flex container.
steps.hint: Set order: -1; on the .item3 selector. Negative values place items before those with order: 0.
steps.expectedOutcome: The third flex item (.item3) will appear first in the visual order due to its negative order value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're setting order: -1; specifically on the .item3 selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're modifying the correct selector (.item3) and using the correct property value (order: -1;).

steps.title: Reset all items to the same order value
steps.instruction: Set the order property to 0 for all three flex items (.item1, .item2, and .item3) to restore their original source order positions.
steps.hint: In CSS, the order property with a value of 0 places items in their natural document flow order. Set order: 0; for each item selector.
steps.expectedOutcome: All three flex items will have order: 0, causing them to appear in their original source order (item1, item2, item3) within the flex container.
successCriteria: The CSS contains order: 0; for .item1, .item2, and .item3 selectors.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've set some items to order: 0, but not all three. Make sure .item1, .item2, and .item3 all have order: 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: The items don't all have order: 0. Check that you've set order: 0; for each item selector to reset their positions.

steps.title: Create a complex ordering scenario
steps.instruction: Update the order values for all three items to create a custom arrangement: set .item1 to order: 3, .item2 to order: 1, and .item3 to order: 2.
steps.hint: Modify the existing order properties in each item's CSS rule to match the specified values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The flex items will be arranged in a custom order based on the new values: item2 (order:1) appears first, item3 (order:2) second, and item1 (order:3) last.
successCriteria: The CSS contains .item1 with order:3, .item2 with order:1, and .item3 with order:2.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've updated some order values, but not all three match the required values. Check that .item1 has order:3, .item2 has order:1, and .item3 has order:2.
steps.feedbackWrong: The order values don't match the required scenario. Ensure you set .item1 to order:3, .item2 to order:1, and .item3 to order:2.

steps.title: Add visual indicators for order values
steps.instruction: Add a pseudo-element to each flex item to visually display its order value using the content property.
steps.hint: Use the ::before or ::after pseudo-element with content property to show the order value as text.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each flex item will show its order value as small text inside it, making the order relationship visually clear.
successCriteria: All three flex item selectors (.item1, .item2, .item3) have a pseudo-element with content property showing their order value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some visual indicators, but not all items have them. Make sure each .item selector has a pseudo-element with content.
steps.feedbackWrong: The visual indicators are missing or incorrect. Add ::before or ::after pseudo-elements with content property to display order values.

steps.title: Add responsive behavior with media queries
steps.instruction: Create a media query that changes the order values for all flex items when the screen width is below 600px.
steps.hint: Use @media (max-width: 600px) to target smaller screens, then override the order properties inside.
steps.expectedOutcome: The flex items will reorder when the screen width is less than 600px, demonstrating responsive order changes.
successCriteria: A media query with max-width: 600px is added and changes the order values for .item1, .item2, and .item3.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a media query, but it may not target all items or change their order values correctly. Check that all .item classes are included inside the media query with new order values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The media query is missing or doesn't correctly change the order values for the flex items. Review the syntax and ensure you're targeting screen widths below 600px.
